meta.disclaimer: Educational encyclopedia samples. Defensive literacy only. SubjectIds point at shared cy_* graph entities.

articles.title: Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228)
articles.summary: A critical remote code execution class of vulnerability in Apache Log4j 2 that became a defining teaching case for dependency risk.
articles.history: Publicly disclosed in December 2021. Widely discussed across vendors and governments as a supply-chain-of-libraries moment.
articles.howItWorks: At a literacy level: certain logging paths could lead to unexpected remote class loading when crafted input was logged. Details belong in vendor advisories — this article does not provide exploit steps.
articles.whyItMatters: Shows why inventory of libraries matters as much as OS patching.

references.label: Shared cyber graph — Log4Shell teaching chain

articles.title: Heartbleed (CVE-2014-0160)
articles.summary: A memory disclosure vulnerability in OpenSSL’s TLS heartbeat extension — a cornerstone of modern disclosure literacy.
articles.history: Disclosed April 2014. Prompted widespread certificate and key rotation guidance.
articles.howItWorks: Literacy only: a bounds-checking failure in heartbeat handling could leak process memory. No exploitation guidance here.
articles.whyItMatters: Illustrates why cryptographic libraries are high-leverage infrastructure.

articles.title: WannaCry
articles.summary: A widely reported ransomware wave associated with EternalBlue-era Windows SMB exposure — used here as an educational case.
articles.history: May 2017 global awareness event. Strongly associated in public reporting with unpatched SMBv1 pathways.
articles.howItWorks: Defensive literacy focuses on patching, network exposure, and backups — not malware internals for offense.
articles.whyItMatters: Connects missing patches to disruptive outcomes without fear marketing.

articles.title: EternalBlue / MS17-010 literacy
articles.summary: A Windows SMBv1 remote code execution class associated with MS17-010 patching — prerequisite literacy for WannaCry/NotPetya teaching.
articles.history: Patch released March 2017; later campaign associations in public reporting.
articles.howItWorks: Discussed only as “unpatched SMBv1 exposure.” No exploit instructions.
articles.whyItMatters: Shows the cost of deferred platform patches.

articles.title: SolarWinds / SUNBURST supply-chain campaign (literacy)
articles.summary: A supply-chain compromise teaching case centered on trusted update channels and vendor software trust.
articles.history: Public discourse intensified in late 2020 around Orion-related compromise narratives.
articles.howItWorks: Educational focus: integrity of software distribution — not actor TTPs for replication.
articles.whyItMatters: Inventory and vendor trust matter beyond CVSS scores.

articles.title: NotPetya (2017) — disruptive malware literacy
articles.summary: A destructive wiper-styled event often discussed alongside EternalBlue-era exposure — continental educational awareness, not precise victim mapping.
articles.history: June 2017 public disruption narratives.
articles.howItWorks: Defensive lessons emphasize patching, segmentation, and backup resilience.
articles.whyItMatters: Distinguishes ransomware-for-profit narratives from destructive disruption.

articles.title: Encryption — defensive literacy
articles.summary: Encryption protects confidentiality and integrity of data in transit and at rest when correctly implemented and keyed.
articles.history: Public-key cryptography and TLS evolved over decades of standards work.
articles.howItWorks: Keys, algorithms, and protocols cooperate; weak configurations undermine strong algorithms.
articles.whyItMatters: Heartbleed-class events show crypto libraries are critical infrastructure.

articles.title: Authentication & MFA
articles.summary: Authentication establishes identity; multi-factor authentication reduces reliance on passwords alone.
articles.history: Passwords → MFA → phishing-resistant authenticators (ongoing).
articles.howItWorks: Something you know / have / are — combined carefully.
articles.whyItMatters: Identity-focused seasons make account recovery and MFA hygiene high leverage.

articles.title: Identity in cybersecurity
articles.summary: Identity binds people and services to permissions; compromise of identity often bypasses other controls.
articles.history: Enterprise identity systems grew with directory and cloud SSO models.
articles.howItWorks: Directories, federation, and least privilege cooperate.
articles.whyItMatters: Many modern incidents begin with credential or session abuse — literacy, not offense.

articles.title: Patching as defensive practice
articles.summary: Patching reduces known defect exposure when inventory and testing allow calm, timely updates.
articles.history: Vendor patch calendars (including Patch Tuesday culture) shaped operational hygiene.
articles.howItWorks: Identify → prioritize → test → deploy → verify.
articles.whyItMatters: EternalBlue-era lessons remain foundational.

articles.title: Software dependency risk
articles.summary: Applications inherit risk from libraries and build pipelines — Log4Shell made this mainstream literacy.
articles.history: Open-source dependency graphs expanded faster than inventory practices in many orgs.
articles.howItWorks: SBOMs and inventory link advisories to what you actually run.
articles.whyItMatters: CVEs on transitive libraries can outrank obvious OS issues.

articles.title: Software supply chain trust
articles.summary: Trust in update channels and build integrity is as important as host hardening.
articles.history: SolarWinds-era discourse elevated supply-chain awareness globally.
articles.howItWorks: Verify publishers, monitor advisories, constrain privileged update paths.
articles.whyItMatters: A trusted pipe can deliver untrusted code.

articles.title: Backups & restore confidence
articles.summary: Backups matter only if restores work — especially in ransomware-awareness seasons.
articles.history: 3-2-1 and immutable backup patterns spread as ransomware themes grew.
articles.howItWorks: Copy → protect → test restore on a schedule.
articles.whyItMatters: Recovery is a defensive control, not an afterthought.

articles.title: Network exposure literacy
articles.summary: Services reachable from untrusted networks inherit extra risk — especially legacy protocols.
articles.history: Internet-facing SMB and RDP themes recur in public guidance.
articles.howItWorks: Reduce attack surface; prefer least exposure; monitor change.
articles.whyItMatters: WannaCry-era lessons start with what is reachable.

articles.title: Cloud security fundamentals
articles.summary: Shared responsibility: providers secure the cloud; customers secure what they configure and place in it.
articles.history: Cloud adoption outpaced identity and logging maturity in many organizations.
articles.howItWorks: Identity, network controls, encryption, and monitoring cooperate.
articles.whyItMatters: Outage seasons and identity seasons both touch cloud estates.

articles.title: Container security literacy
articles.summary: Containers package apps with dependencies — inheritance of library risk still applies.
articles.history: Container adoption accelerated developer velocity and inventory challenges.
articles.howItWorks: Images, registries, runtime isolation, and least privilege.
articles.whyItMatters: Log4j-class libraries can ship inside images unnoticed.

articles.title: Virtualization hygiene
articles.summary: Hypervisors and guests need patching and access control like any other platform.
articles.history: Home labs and enterprises alike concentrate risk in virtualization hosts.
articles.howItWorks: Separate management planes; keep guests inventoried.
articles.whyItMatters: A compromised host can affect many workloads.

articles.title: Linux workstation literacy
articles.summary: Linux desktops still need updates, least privilege, and careful remote access.
articles.history: Linux security culture emphasizes packages, permissions, and transparency.
articles.howItWorks: Distro updates, user separation, firewall defaults.
articles.whyItMatters: OpenSSL and other shared libraries sit under many stacks.

articles.title: Browser security literacy
articles.summary: Browsers are high-frequency update surfaces; extensions expand trust boundaries.
articles.history: Browser vendors ship rapid security updates as a primary defense.
articles.howItWorks: Sandboxing, auto-updates, extension review.
articles.whyItMatters: Browser seasons call for calm update cadence — not panic.

articles.title: Security frameworks (NIST CSF literacy)
articles.summary: Frameworks organize defensive practice without prescribing offensive tactics.
articles.history: NIST Cybersecurity Framework popularized Identify–Protect–Detect–Respond–Recover language.
articles.howItWorks: Map controls to outcomes; measure calmly.
articles.whyItMatters: Gives structure to playbooks and posture discussions.

articles.title: CIS Controls literacy
articles.summary: Prioritized defensive practices for common environments — educational orientation only.
articles.history: CIS Controls evolved as a practical baseline conversation.
articles.howItWorks: Implement safeguards appropriate to your size and risk.
articles.whyItMatters: Helps small orgs avoid random tool shopping.

articles.title: Java ecosystem security literacy
articles.summary: Java apps often pull logging and web libraries — dependency inventory is essential.
articles.history: Log4Shell elevated Java dependency awareness worldwide.
articles.howItWorks: Build tools resolve transitive jars; operators must know what ships.
articles.whyItMatters: Language choice does not remove patch duty.

articles.title: Developer tools & secrets hygiene
articles.summary: IDEs, CI, and package managers are part of the trust boundary.
articles.history: Shift-left culture added security checks earlier in delivery.
articles.howItWorks: Pin versions, scan dependencies, protect secrets — defensively.
articles.whyItMatters: Build systems can become supply-chain chokepoints.
